A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSPulse work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original TSPulse results for anomaly detection, classification, imputation and retrieval, together with ablations, embedding analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds comparisons across embedding types, retrieval ablations, a unified-checkpoint evaluation and simulated missingness experiments.

M1.justification: The masked time/FFT inputs, TSMixer backbone, register tokens, reconstruction objectives, TSLens and multi-head triangulation remain. The three-view terminology and signature/prediction head names reframe existing components. Optional head pruning was already documented in v2 Appendix A.6; the unified-checkpoint experiment evaluates an existing variant.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpora, four tasks and existing benchmark datasets are retained. v3 Appendix A.16 adds seven simulated ETTh1 scenarios labeled MAR or MNAR, introducing channel-, value- and time-dependent missingness beyond the earlier block/hybrid masking conditions.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds GPT4TS/OFA and UniTS to the runtime comparison in v2 Table 23. v2 explicitly excluded UniTS from that experiment. Comparator membership in the retained task-performance tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces substantial additional evaluation designs: quantitative comparisons across three embedding types, including 2,000 sampled instances for missingness analysis; one checkpoint evaluated across tasks; retrieval component controls; and seven conditional missingness simulations. Existing benchmark splits, masking ratios, tuning procedures and runtime measurement settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's register-embedding PCA and existing task ablations, v3 adds controlled comparisons of temporal, spectral and semantic sensitivity (Section 6/A.3), retrieval masking/embedding ablations (Table 26), task-specialization analysis (Table 30), and MAR/MNAR robustness tests (Table 31). These address several previously untested questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The DuckDuckGeese cross-validation description is retained, and the new results continue to use point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched existing benchmark values are unchanged, including classification mean accuracy 0.733. Substantial new results include retrieval PREC@3 of 0.645 versus 0.496 without hybrid pretraining (Table 26), unified-checkpoint classification accuracy 0.71 versus task-specialized 0.73 (Table 30), and MAR S1 MSE 0.147 versus MOMENT's 0.575 (Table 31), plus embedding-distortion and additional runtime results.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A.3 introduces explicit mathematical definitions of mask-, noise- and phase-induced embedding distortion in Equations 1–3. These were absent from v2's qualitative sensitivity analysis. Existing reconstruction losses and anomaly-score mathematics remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 extends the detailed-versus-semantic disentanglement framing to explicit claims about differentiated temporal, spectral and semantic response properties, listed as an emergent-representation contribution. The compact model, four supported tasks, headline performance gains and GPU-free deployment claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 6/A.3 newly interprets differences among embedding types as evidence of disentanglement and connects their sensitivities to downstream roles. Appendices A.15–A.16 add interpretations about transfer without task specialization and robustness through reduced pretraining mask bias. The earlier limitations and future-work discussion is retained in A.17.

D1.justification: v3 supplies setup details for the added analyses and corrects the inverse FFT API reference to torch.fft.irfft. It replaces v2's contradictory reviewer-ZIP/post-review disclosure with a public reproducibility statement, although v2 already linked the same model page. Some details are removed, including the task-dependent UniTS size discussion; principal hyperparameters and hardware remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted positioning against TimeDRL, TF-C and cross-reconstruction work, distinguishing joint disentanglement across spaces and abstraction levels. Rubin (1976) is added for missingness, while Time-LLM and LLMTime references are removed. The broader positioning around compact, transferable time-series pretraining remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around diagnostic tasks and disentanglement. Workflows gain numbered subsections, terminology changes throughout, and the appendix gains a contents list and substantial reordering that brings runtime and sensitivity analyses forward. Citation style and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: v3 revises Figures 1–3, adds summary and detailed analysis tables, expands and relocates the runtime table, and substantially rearranges existing displays under ICLR formatting. The earlier PCA plots are retained with different numbering and placement; existing benchmark tables are mostly reformatted or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the existing design through comparisons across embedding types, retrieval component ablations and the unified-checkpoint evaluation (Section 6; Tables 26 and 30), while Table 31 broadens missingness testing. These meaningfully extend v2's already extensive evaluation. The gains remain limited by indirect support for the stronger disentanglement claims and missingness evidence confined to ETTh1 without uncertainty estimates.
